assumptions: The requested slider accepts a broad control that follows an arcuate guide while remaining integral to one wing; this resolves the exact three-part constraint without a fourth prismatic body.
Assembly may be a deliberate two-hand action even though normal transformation and reset must be discoverable and one-handed.
Rigid tool-free capture may be deliberately reversible only through coordinated lift-and-rotate service motion outside the intended planar operating cycle.
A common 0.4 mm-nozzle FDM printer and one rigid filament are the baseline; exact shrink, friction, surface finish, and force remain Make/physical questions.
Nominal clearances are parameterized design gaps, not universal printer capability or physical proof.

components.form: A 78 by 54 mm low crescent plate with a 4.0 mm backing, rounded perimeter, two vertical journals, a guarded common-plane gear tunnel, a 15 mm-radius thumb-track opening, two 8 mm entry lips, and six fixed moon-skin bridges. Each root has a raised service shelf from absolute 118 through the 82-degree stop land to a paired vertical drop window at 78 degrees. No service-sector underside is below Z=9.2 mm; a 1.6 mm-thick 45-degree-tented high hood and side cheeks guard the tooth mesh while clearing the raised top by 0.50 mm. Low operating capture roofs begin at 76 degrees, after the roots are seated, and continue through closed.
components.interfaces: Each 5.0 mm journal ends in a 7.4 mm-diameter, 1.2 mm-high mushroom flange and runs in a 5.6 mm wing bearing bore with 0.30 mm nominal radial clearance per side. A 7.8 mm service lobe and 6.0 mm connecting throat admit that flange only at mirrored +/-118 degrees. Service shelves hold both roots 1.2 mm above operation from 118 to the 78-degree paired drop windows; fixed service hoods and flange undersides are Z=9.2 mm or higher. The raised state crosses the 82-degree stop lands with 0.20 mm nominal clearance above 1.0 mm axial lug engagement. At 78 degrees both roots descend vertically 1.2 mm on the operating side of the lands; low roofs and guide cheeks begin at 76 degrees with 0.50 mm nominal roof clearance and continue through closed. Two complete module-1.0, 18-tooth gears have 9.0 mm pitch radii, 18 mm center spacing, 0.40 mm nominal total flank backlash, 0.25 mm tip relief, and 0.35 mm 45-degree axial lead chamfers. Teeth remain meshed through service, drop, operation, and reset.
components.name: Crescent pebble chassis with inside-stop paired-drop pockets
components.placement: Front view is XY and pivot axes are parallel to Z. Pivot centers are X=+/-9.0 mm and Y=-7.5 mm, 18 mm apart. Mirrored signed wing angles have equal absolute value. The lower 24 mm of the convex rim is a fixed grip zone at least 15 mm from either swept wing edge.
components.purpose: Provides the smooth resting form, fixed pivots, high-guarded raised service sectors, paired drop windows, low guarded operating pockets, hard stops, aperture backing, moon-skin bridges, grip island, and all retention geometry.

components.form: A 3.0 mm rigid swept wing web with a complete rounded 18-tooth root gear, keyed 5.6/7.8/6.0 mm bearing aperture, three radiused five-point through-stars measuring 5.5, 6.5, and 7.0 mm across their outer points, two shallow vein ribs, an 18 by 12 by 2.2 mm rounded thumb shoe, and a shallow 12 mm-diameter textured press moon outside the guarded root. The perimeter is a rounded crescent forewing with no sharp point.
components.interfaces: Its service lobe passes over the left flange only at +118 degrees. After both gears mesh at timing marks, its root remains at Z=5.7-8.7 mm while its raised stop lug crosses the +82-degree land, then descends vertically with the right root to Z=4.5-7.5 mm at +78 degrees. The press moon is at least 12 mm from tooth mesh. In operation the complete gear stays engaged with the right gear; broad stop shoulders, not teeth, set 0 and 82 degrees.
components.name: Left moon-moth wing with integral thumb slider and press moon
components.placement: On the left journal. Closed at 0 degrees it stays inside the 78 by 54 mm chassis projection; seated operation rotates it to +82 degrees. Its thumb shoe follows a 15 mm-radius, 82-degree arcuate window for 21.5 mm nominal travel. The service gate and paired drop window are +118 and +78 degrees; low capture roof starts inboard at +76 degrees.
components.purpose: Forms the left half of the closed pebble and deployed moth, supplies the only normal-use control, drives the right wing, and provides one broad two-hand assembly press zone without becoming another part.

components.form: A mirror 3.0 mm swept wing web and complete 18-tooth root gear with the same keyed bearing aperture, three star apertures, rounded perimeter, structural ribs, axial tooth lead chamfers, and 12 mm textured assembly press moon, but without the thumb-shoe arm. A shallow crescent relief balances the closed face.
components.interfaces: Its service lobe passes over the right flange only at -118 degrees and it remains raised while the left root is loaded. Equal complete gears mesh at engraved timing dots; both raised lugs cross their -/+82-degree lands, then the right root descends synchronously with the left at -/+78 degrees. Its 1.0 mm seated stop-lug engagement and low operating roof mirror the left interfaces; both seating witness lines must be flush before normal cycling.
components.name: Right moon-moth driven wing with press moon
components.placement: On the right journal. Closed at 0 degrees it remains inside the chassis projection and seated operation rotates it to -82 degrees. Its service gate and paired drop window are -118 and -78 degrees; low capture roof starts inboard at -76 degrees.
components.purpose: Completes the closed pebble and mirrored deployed silhouette, follows the left wing positively, and supplies the second broad assembly press zone while remaining one rigid printed part.

distinctive_features: A calm crescent pebble silhouette expands to roughly 2.5 times its closed width.
Six five-point openings appear as true negative space only after leaving fixed moon-skin bridges and backing.
The broad moon-notch control follows the crescent instead of adding a protruding knob.
Two equal root gears make bilateral cooperation inspectable through one guarded window.
Two subtle assembly press moons, paired 78-degree drop marks, and seating lines make the one-time service ingress legible without adding parts.
concept.intended_interaction: Rest the closed crescent across the fingers with the thumb in its concave notch. Push the 20 by 11 mm pad along the engraved crescent track until the open hard stop: the left root drives the identical right root 1:1, so both seated wings sweep outward together and the six masked star apertures become open negative space. Keep fingers on the raised rear grip island, outside the marked lateral sweep. Push the same pad back to the closed stop. Normal use is one-handed, planar, reversible, and requires no lift, shake, separate reset, spring, or forced flex.

motion_and_geometry.assembly_height_function: For raised service motion 78<=abs(q)<=118 degrees, both moving root/gear intervals are Z=[5.7,8.7] mm. At abs(q)=78 degrees both roots descend vertically by 1.2 mm to Z=[4.5,7.5] mm. For seated motion from 78 to 0, and for intended normal planar operation 0<=abs(q)<=82, Z=[4.5,7.5] mm.
assembly_sequence: Place the chassis back-down. Load the right root at -118 degrees through its unique service lobe and leave it on the raised shelf.
Load the left root at +118 degrees; align engraved timing dots; mesh both complete gears while raised.
Hold only the two rounded outer press moons and counter-rotate both raised roots across the +/-82-degree stop lands to the +/-78-degree drop marks.
At +/-78 degrees press both zones evenly toward the chassis by 1.2 mm until both seating lines are flush; do not press one wing alone.
Rotate seated inward past the +/-76-degree low-roof entries, continue to 0 with the left shoe, and confirm both closed stops before normal cycling.
motion_and_geometry.degrees_of_freedom: Normal use has one intended planar degree of freedom. The left integral shoe rotates its root, and equal complete external gears constrain the right root to equal-and-opposite angle. Assembly adds one coordinated two-hand axial input only at the marked 78-degree paired service windows.
motion_and_geometry.deliberate_disassembly: Tool-free disassembly intentionally aligns both roots at +/-78 degrees, lifts both together by 1.2 mm through the concealed paired windows, counter-rotates outward across the +/-82-degree stop lands while raised, and continues to the +/-118-degree service lobes. The wings remain retained under the mushroom flanges throughout intended one-handed planar cycling; they are not claimed to be permanently nondisassemblable under coordinated service action.
motion_and_geometry.hard_stops: Broad 4.8 by 6.0 mm root shoulders contact integral chassis lands at 0 and 82 degrees. Each seated lug overlaps its open land by 1.0 mm axially; at 1.2 mm service height it clears by 0.20 mm nominally so assembly can cross the land before dropping at 78 degrees. Teeth never serve as stops.
motion_and_geometry.operating_range: Both roots remain seated for intended planar motion from 0 through 82 degrees absolute wing angle. The assembly path crosses 82 while raised, drops on the operating side at 78, and therefore never asks a seated feature to cross the hard-stop wall.
states_to_check: 118 degrees service: sequential lobe entry plus 0.50 mm clearance to flange and high-guard undersides.
94, 88, 84, and 82 degrees service: both roots remain raised, stop lugs clear lands, gears stay timed, and every overhead underside remains at or above Z=9.2 mm.
78 degrees paired drop: both roots align with concealed vertical windows on the operating side of the stop lands and descend 1.2 mm without tooth disengagement.
76 degrees capture entry: both roots are fully seated before entering low roofs with 0.50 mm nominal clearance.
82 degrees operating open: when approached seated from inside, both stop contacts are simultaneous and ordinary planar force cannot cross toward service.
62, 41, 20, and 18 degrees: seated gear engagement, bridge release, sweep gaps, and entry-lip approach.
0 degrees closed: both stop shoulders seated, wings inside the chassis silhouette, and all six stars over backing beneath moon-skin bridges.
motion_and_geometry.travel: Each operating wing rotates 82 degrees; thumb-shoe travel is 15*radians(82)=21.5 mm. Assembly raised rotation is 40 degrees from 118 to 78, including a 4-degree raised crossing beyond the 82-degree stop; seated ingress to low roofs is 2 degrees from 78 to 76.

concept.object_and_category: A one-handed, hand-powered transforming desk toy: a rounded crescent pebble that becomes a planar moon-moth silhouette through one reversible arcuate thumb-slide. Assembly and deliberate disassembly are separate two-hand service actions.
concept.print_stance: The chassis prints broad smooth back on the bed. Its service shelves and paired drop pockets are upward-facing; the high service hood and low operating lips use 45-degree tent profiles with no horizontal roof span above 4 mm. Each wing prints flat on its inner face with journal axis vertical, through-stars vertical, pad face upward, ribs upward, and tooth lead chamfers support-facing at 45 degrees. All three stances are support-free candidates for a 0.4 mm nozzle, subject to exact slicer inspection in Make; no successful print is claimed at Invent.
concept.safety_strategy: No stored energy, normal-use axial input, or forced flex is intended. From 0 through 76 degrees, low roofs and guide cheeks limit axial play and cover the complete gear mesh. From 76 through the 82-degree open endpoint, mushroom flanges retain both roots, high tented gear hoods and side cheeks block fingertip access to the mesh, and seated stop lands block planar travel toward release; the broad shoe supplies rotation but no paired lifting purchase. The lower 24 mm grip island remains at least 15 mm from swept wing edges. At each body-side entrance, an 8 mm overlapping lip has underside Z=8.0 mm; in the last 18 degrees the already-seated moving edge is at least 5 mm under that lip with 0.50 mm roof clearance. The two assembly press moons are outside the guards and at least 12 mm from tooth mesh. Make must probe all hood/press-zone openings and the 76-to-82-degree transition for accidental lift and finger access; no child-safety certification is claimed.
concept.signature_decision: Retain the three-part equal-gear transformation, but replace the rejected raised-to-closed drop with an inside-stop paired-drop service path. Both complete gears remain meshed while raised stop lugs pass the 82-degree lands; broad outer press zones lower both roots at 78 degrees, and two degrees of seated inward rotation place them under low capture roofs. Normal use remains one planar 0-to-82-degree motion; deliberate service reversal requires coordinated two-hand lift and outward rotation.
concept.summary: A palm-size crescent chassis and two retained rigid wings form exactly three printed parts. Closed, both wings lie within a backed crescent face while fixed moon-skin bridges cover six tiny star apertures. A broad shoe integral to the left wing drives equal complete root gears, counter-rotating both wings through 82 degrees into a 136 mm moth silhouette. For tool-free assembly, both roots rotate raised from mirrored 118-degree loading gates across the 82-degree stop lands, descend together by 1.2 mm at marked 78-degree windows on the operating side, and enter low capture roofs by 76 degrees before approaching any entry lip or moon-skin bridge.
concept.title: Moon-Moth Bloom — Inside-Stop Starplug Crescent
unresolved_risks: The inside-stop paired-drop sequence is specified kinematically but not yet built; Make must prove both raised roots cross their stop lands, align at 78 degrees, descend together without tooth disengagement, and enter the 76-degree low roofs without collision or asymmetric seating.

Gear backlash may let one 78-degree drop window align before the other; Make must test both backlash extremes, seating-line mismatch, tooth lead chamfers, and whether two-hand pressure can seat both roots without a jam.
The 0.20 mm nominal raised stop-lug clearance is a starting dimension, not a proven FDM fit; Make must tune it while retaining positive seated overlap.

The marked 78-degree pose lies inside the normal angular sweep and deliberately permits paired axial service lift; Make must show the broad one-hand shoe supplies no axial purchase, the roots remain under their flanges, and ordinary handling does not initiate the coordinated release path.

Paired vertical seating may feel fussy; Make must verify the high service hoods block a conservative fingertip probe while leaving both marked press zones usable. No physical force, jam, wear, cycle, inversion, or human-discovery evidence exists yet.
The 136 mm open width is desk-scale but wider than the closed palm form; Make must confirm swept envelope and desk stability.
concept.wall_and_edge_plan: Wing webs and root-gear faces are 3.0 mm axially; wing perimeter and aperture ligaments are at least 2.4 mm; stop shoulders are at least 4.8 by 6.0 mm; stop-lug axial engagement is 1.0 mm; journals are 5.0 mm diameter; chassis backing is 4.0 mm; low operating root walls and roofs are 2.4 mm. The high service gear hood is a 1.6 mm 45-degree tent with 2.4 mm side cheeks and no unsupported horizontal span above 4 mm; its top remains at Z=10.8 mm inside the 11 mm envelope. Gear faces receive 0.35 mm 45-degree axial lead chamfers. Exterior touch edges use at least 2.0 mm radii and wing tips use 4-7 mm radii.
concept.z_stack_and_assembly: Z=0 is the chassis back. Backing occupies Z=0-4.0 mm. In normal operation both wing webs and complete gears occupy Z=4.5-7.5 mm; fixed operating roof, entry-lip, and moon-skin-bridge undersides are Z=8.0 mm and roofs end by Z=10.4 mm, preserving 0.50 mm nominal roof clearance. For raised service motion from abs(q)=118 through 78 degrees, both moving stacks occupy Z=5.7-8.7 mm; mushroom-flange and high service-hood undersides are at least Z=9.2 mm, preserving 0.50 mm. Load right at -118, then left at +118; mesh at timing dots; counter-rotate raised across the +/-82-degree stop lands to +/-78; press both broad outer wing zones so the roots descend together 1.2 mm through paired windows to Z=4.5-7.5 mm; confirm both seating lines; then rotate seated past the +/-76-degree low-roof entries and continue to 0. The moving stack is below Z=8.0 before entering any low roof, lip, or bridge. No seated feature crosses a stop. No glue, pin, screw, magnet, string, support removal, forced flex, or snap is part of assembly.

alternatives_considered.advantage: Literal straight slider and visually pure symmetry.
alternatives_considered.family: Central translating dual-cam slider with two mutually hinged wing shells
alternatives_considered.rejection_reason: With exactly three physical parts there is no independent frame; hinge, linear guide, axial capture, and fixed reference collapse into a stacked interlock with higher assembly and jam risk.

alternatives_considered.advantage: Few fine features and a broad push surface.
alternatives_considered.family: Central wedge slider spreading two wing-shell halves
alternatives_considered.rejection_reason: A wedge positively opens but does not positively synchronize return, and its behavior depends on grip friction and shell squeeze.

alternatives_considered.advantage: Simple vertical transition with large separation from the final closing lips.
alternatives_considered.family: Full drop at 90 degrees, then rotate seated to the 82-degree stop
alternatives_considered.rejection_reason: A seated stop shoulder would have to cross the fixed 82-degree stop from its forbidden side; changing angular offsets does not remove that topological collision.

alternatives_considered.advantage: Directly avoids the cited low-lip collision.
alternatives_considered.family: Full drop at 24 degrees before the final 18-degree lip interval
alternatives_considered.rejection_reason: It puts a reversible full-lift window inside every normal 0-to-82-degree operating cycle, weakening capture.

alternatives_considered.family: Raise every guard, lip, and bridge above the 8.7 mm service top
alternatives_considered.rejection_reason: A 2.4 mm roof would reach at least Z=11.6 and would leave about 1.7 mm operating axial space, weakening the low pebble read, close guarding, and axial control.

alternatives_considered.advantage: No seated stop crossing and a short service path.
alternatives_considered.family: Full drop at the 82-degree open endpoint
alternatives_considered.rejection_reason: The operating endpoint itself becomes a full reversible lift window and paired timing is sensitive to gear backlash.

alternatives_considered.advantage: Combines rotation and descent while keeping both gears engaged.
alternatives_considered.family: Mirrored helical descent ending seated exactly at the 82-degree stop
alternatives_considered.rejection_reason: The ramp still ends on the service side of the hard-stop wall; a root cannot become seated at that wall and then cross into the 0-to-82-degree operating side.

alternatives_considered.advantage: Both complete gears remain positively meshed, raised lugs cross the 82-degree stop lands before descent, and both roots seat before entering low roofs at 76 degrees.
alternatives_considered.family: Raised stop crossing followed by paired vertical drop at 78 degrees
alternatives_considered.selection_reason: This is the only compared path that preserves the three parts, 82-degree silhouette, low guarded operating stack, tool-free rigid assembly, support-free chassis stance, and a continuous stop topology while directly eliminating the host-proven 0.7 mm collision.

design_calculations: Equal external gears at 18 mm center spacing and 9 mm pitch radii impose equal-magnitude opposite angular motion; both roots remain coplanar because they share one raised plane, one paired vertical drop, and one operating plane.

Raised rotation is 118-78=40 degrees. The raised roots cross 4 degrees beyond the 82-degree stop lands before descent; the seated roots rotate 2 degrees farther inward before low roofs begin at 76 degrees; the drop remains 60 degrees from the final 18-degree lip interval.

Nominal 0.40 mm total flank backlash at 9 mm pitch radius is 0.04444 radians or 2.546 degrees. Make must sweep that phase range against both 78-degree drop windows rather than infer simultaneous alignment.

The service top 8.7 mm remains 0.50 mm below the 9.2 mm flange underside; the seated top 7.5 mm remains 0.50 mm below operating roofs at 8.0 mm; a 1.0 mm seated stop-lug engagement leaves 0.20 mm nominal clearance when raised by 1.2 mm.
Thumb travel remains 15*radians(82)=21.5 mm; two 58 mm pivot-to-tip reaches at 82 degrees plus 18 mm pivot spacing are about 132.8 mm, within the 136 mm envelope.

repair_binding.addressed_by: Both raised roots now cross the 82-degree stop lands and descend together at 78 degrees through paired windows on the operating side. They enter low capture roofs only after seating, at 76 degrees, and therefore never enter fixed geometry beginning at Z=8.0 while raised.

research.scope: Source-backed FDM starting points, explicit geometric calculations, and a selected-Inventor repair review. Sources support general modeling choices only; arithmetic establishes internal design consistency only; neither proves manufactured fit, safety, force, wear, or user response.

sources.application: Keep wing stances flat, make service shelves and drop pockets upward-facing, use 45-degree tented edges, retain adjustable 0.50 mm moving-clearance baselines, and require slicer and CAD checks rather than treating guidance as proof.
sources.supported_claims: FFF layers need support beneath them; short bridges can print, ordinary support-free overhang guidance is roughly 45-60 degrees, a common nozzle is 0.4 mm, no fit tolerance is universal, and at least 0.3 mm is presented as an initial moving-part value.
sources.title: Modeling with 3D printing in mind

sources.application: Use thicker 2.4-6.0 mm structural paths, 0.50 mm initial moving gaps, and 45-degree support-facing chamfers as conservative design decisions, not certified limits.
sources.supported_claims: The article presents 1.2 mm as a good FDM minimum-wall starting point for a typical 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.5 mm spacing for separated parts, and 45-degree FDM support-free overhang guidance.
sources.title: SolidWorks Tutorial: Modeling and Inspection Masterclass for 3D Printing

specialist_review.conclusion: Reject both a full drop at 90 degrees and a helical descent ending seated at the 82-degree stop because a seated feature cannot cross that stop wall. Keep the roots raised across 82, perform a paired drop at 78, preserve deliberate-disassembly caveats, and require Make to sweep backlash extremes and service poses.

verification_required_in_make: Create source-first parametric CAD with exactly three product parts and explicit assembly/service and normal operating configurations.

Check raised service at 118, 94, 88, 84, and 82 degrees; paired-drop alignment at 78; capture-roof entry at 76; and seated operation at 82, 62, 41, 20, 18, and 0 degrees at both backlash extremes. Report intersections, root heights, roof/flange clearances, stop overlap, tooth-face overlap, and seating-line mismatch.

Demonstrate sequential loading, complete-gear timing, raised crossing of both open-stop lands, simultaneous 1.2 mm drop on the operating side, seated entry under low roofs, and deliberate reverse disassembly distinct from normal planar operation.
Run validity, exact three-part inventory, wall/ligament thickness, gear contact, hard-stop timing, fingertip-probe, swept-envelope, and interference checks from exact geometry.
Slice each declared stance with supports disabled and preserve orientation evidence; a slicer preview is not a successful print.

Render service 118, raised stop crossing 82, paired drop 78, captured 76, seated open 82, operating intermediate 41, closed 0, and exploded states; inspect access, root guarding, star masking, and closed pebble read.
Keep physical fit, force, feel, wear, cycle life, safety certification, and human discovery explicitly unverified without corresponding real evidence.
